# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
for (nm in c("Ji_2020_benapenem", "Ji_2020_benapenem_mouse")) {
  ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(nm))
  cat("**", nm, "**\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("* Citation: ", ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("* Description: ", ui$description, "\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.01751-19>

Benapenem is a carbapenem developed for infections caused by
Enterobacteriaceae, including ESBL-producing strains. Ji and colleagues used a
model-informed approach to choose a clinical regimen and a PK/PD
susceptibility cutoff. The paper has four modelling pieces, all fitted in
NONMEM 7 by FOCE-I:

1. **Mouse popPK** (`Ji_2020_benapenem_mouse`). A two-compartment model for
   single IV bolus doses of 1.9 to 233 mg/kg in neutropenic thigh-infected
   mice. Clearance and central volume both rise with the dose,
   `CL = 0.913 x [1 + (dose / 58.4)^1.46]` mL/h and
   `V1 = 3.62 x [1 + (dose / 58.4)^1.06]` mL (Equations 1 and 2).
2. **Human popPK** (`Ji_2020_benapenem`). A two-compartment model for 250,
   500 and 1,000 mg 30-min IV infusions in 12 healthy volunteers.
   `CL = 0.825 x (dose / 250)^0.183` L/h and
   `V1 = 5.03 x (dose / 250)^0.184 x (WT / 70)` L (Equations 3 and 4), with an
   estimated infusion duration of 0.404 h.
3. **Plasma protein binding**, one fit per species. A two-site model,
   `Cb = Bmax x Cu / (C50 + Cu) + slope x Cu` (Equation 9), converts the
   total concentration to the unbound concentration through the positive
   root of a quadratic (Equations 10 to 12). Both model files carry their
   species' binding parameters and return the unbound concentration as
   `Cunbound`.
4. **PK/PD.** The authors related %fT>MIC, fCmax/MIC and fAUC/MIC in the
   mice to the 24-h change in log10 CFU per gram of thigh. They chose
   %fT>MIC as the index and set targets of 40% (bacteriostatic) and 60%
   (bactericidal). Those relationships are straight trend lines through
   per-strain data (Figures S1 to S12), with no tabulated parameters, so they
   are not packaged. The targets are used below for the probability of target
   attainment (PTA).

Benapenem exposure rises less than in proportion to dose in both species. The
authors attribute this to saturable plasma protein binding: more drug is
unbound at higher concentrations and is cleared faster.

# Population

**Mice.** Male and female ICR mice aged 5 to 6 weeks were made neutropenic
with cyclophosphamide (150 then 100 mg/kg intraperitoneally, 3 days apart) and
infected in the thigh with *Escherichia coli* ATCC 25922 (ESBL-negative). Two
hours later they received a single tail-vein dose of 1.9, 14.6, 58.4 or
233 mg/kg. Six mice were sampled at each of 10 times from 0 to 24 h. Body
weights and the number of mice are not reported.

**Humans.** The benapenem phase I trial enrolled 12 healthy Chinese
volunteers: 6 female and 6 male, median age 28 years (range 21-35), median
weight 61.5 kg (51.8-78.3) and median height 165.3 cm (153.5-181) (Table 1).
They received single 250, 500 or 1,000 mg doses as 30-min IV infusions, with
sampling to 48 h.

The same information is available programmatically via each model's
`population` metadata, for example
`readModelDb("Ji_2020_benapenem")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each
`ini()` entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Ji_2020_benapenem.R` and
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Ji_2020_benapenem_mouse.R`. The table below
collects them in one place.

| Model | Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|-------|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| mouse | `lcl` | log(0.913) mL/h | Table 3 CL; Equation 1 |
| mouse | `lvc` | log(3.62) mL | Table 3 V1; Equation 2 |
| mouse | `lq` | log(0.09) mL/h | Table 3 Q |
| mouse | `lvp` | log(1.65) mL | Table 3 V2 |
| mouse | `e_dose_cl` | 1.46 | Table 3 Dose_CL; Equation 1 |
| mouse | `e_dose_vc` | 1.06 | Table 3 Dose_V1; Equation 2 |
| mouse | `etalcl` | log(1 + 0.365^2) | Table 3 IIV_CL 36.5 |
| mouse | `propSd` | 0.301 | Table 3 Prop. error 30.1% (additive fixed to 0) |
| mouse | `lbmax`, `lkd`, `kns` | log(164), log(0.232), 1.02 | Table 5, mouse row |
| human | `lcl` | log(0.825) L/h | Table 4 CL; Equation 3 |
| human | `lvc` | log(5.03) L | Table 4 V1; Equation 4 |
| human | `lq` | log(1.14) L/h | Table 4 Q |
| human | `lvp` | log(2.93) L | Table 4 V2 |
| human | `ld1` | log(0.404) h | Table 4 D1 |
| human | `e_dose_cl` | 0.183 | Table 4 Dose_CL; Equation 3 |
| human | `e_dose_vc` | 0.184 | Table 4 Dose_V1; Equation 4 |
| human | `(WT / 70)` on V1 | exponent 1 | Equation 4 |
| human | `etalcl`, `etalvc` | log(1 + 0.105^2), log(1 + 0.076^2) | Table 4 IIV_CL 10.5, IIV_V1 7.6 |
| human | `propSd`, `addSd` | 0.074, 0.233 mg/L | Table 4 Prop. error 7.4%, Add. error 0.233 |
| human | `lbmax`, `lkd`, `kns` | log(115), log(8.63), 0.666 | Table 5, human row |
| both | IIV form | `P = Ppop x exp(eta)` | Equation 5 |
| both | Residual error | `Cobs = Cpred x (1 + eps1) + eps2` | Equation 6 |
| both | `Cunbound` | positive root of `a Cu^2 + b Cu + c = 0` | Equations 9-12 |
| both | Two-compartment ODEs | n/a | Results, "PK/PD model and mouse and human Pop-PK models" |

# Protein binding

The bound concentration is a saturable high-affinity term plus a linear
low-affinity term. The figure below redraws Figure 5 from the Table 5
parameters. Its curves pass through the end points of the published curves:
about 565 ug/mL bound at 390 ug/mL unbound in mouse plasma, and about
310 ug/mL bound at 300 ug/mL unbound in human plasma.

```{r binding}
bind_par <- tibble::tribble(
  ~species, ~bmax, ~kd,   ~kns,
  "Mouse",  164,   0.232, 1.02,
  "Human",  115,   8.63,  0.666
)
bound_curve <- tidyr::crossing(bind_par, cu = seq(0, 400, by = 1)) |>
  mutate(cb = bmax * cu / (kd + cu) + kns * cu) |>
  filter(species == "Mouse" | cu <= 300)

ggplot(bound_curve, aes(cu, cb)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~species, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    x = "Free drug concentration (ug/mL)",
    y = "Bound drug concentration (ug/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates the model curves of Figure 5 of Ji 2020."
  )
```

The models take the total concentration and must recover the unbound one. To
check that inversion, the next chunk passes a grid of known unbound
concentrations through Equation 10 to get totals. It then gives each total as
a bolus into the typical 5.03 L central volume (250 mg, 70 kg) of the packaged
human model and checks that `Cunbound` at time 0 returns the starting value.
Both sides use the same parameters, so any difference is floating-point error
and the bound is tight.

```{r binding-roundtrip}
# Typical-value solves of several subjects use zeroRe(), for which rxode2's
# "multi-subject simulation without 'omega'" warning is expected.
solve_typical <- function(model, events) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(model), events, returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

mod_h <- readModelDb("Ji_2020_benapenem")
hb <- bind_par[bind_par$species == "Human", ]
cu_grid <- c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 5, 20, 100, 300)
ct_grid <- cu_grid + hb$bmax * cu_grid / (hb$kd + cu_grid) + hb$kns * cu_grid

ev_rt <- data.frame(
  id = rep(seq_along(ct_grid), each = 2), time = 0, evid = c(1, 0),
  amt = as.vector(rbind(ct_grid * 5.03, 0)), cmt = "central",
  WT = 70, DOSE_BENAPENEM_MG = 250
)
rt <- solve_typical(mod_h, ev_rt)
stopifnot(
  nrow(rt) == length(cu_grid),
  all(abs(rt$Cc / ct_grid - 1) < 1e-10),
  all(abs(rt$Cunbound / cu_grid - 1) < 1e-8)
)

binding_tab <- data.frame(
  unbound = cu_grid,
  total = signif(ct_grid, 4),
  fu_pct = round(100 * cu_grid / ct_grid, 1)
)
knitr::kable(
  binding_tab |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Unbound (ug/mL)" = unbound,
      "Total (ug/mL)" = total,
      "Unbound (%)" = fu_pct
    ),
  caption = "Human plasma: total concentration and unbound percentage for a grid of unbound concentrations."
)
fu_pct <- binding_tab$fu_pct
```

Human benapenem is about `r fu_pct[1]`% unbound at low concentrations and
about `r fu_pct[length(fu_pct)]`% unbound at 300 ug/mL unbound. The authors'
in vitro binding table (Table S2) shows the same saturation, with the bound
fraction falling from about 92% to 50% as the concentration rises.

# Mouse PK (Figure 3)

```{r mouse-c0, include = FALSE}
mouse_wt_kg <- 0.020
mouse_doses <- c(1.9, 14.6, 58.4, 233)
# Equation 2: V1 = 3.62 * [1 + (dose / 58.4)^1.06] mL; amount in ug.
c0_typ_m <- mouse_doses * mouse_wt_kg * 1000 / (3.62 * (1 + (mouse_doses / 58.4)^1.06))
```

The dose records hold the amount per mouse. The paper does not report body
weights, so a 20 g mouse is assumed: the amount in ug is the mg/kg dose times
20. With that weight the typical initial concentrations (dose over V1) are
`r paste(round(c0_typ_m), collapse = ", ")` mg/L for 1.9, 14.6, 58.4 and
233 mg/kg. Each sits inside the spread of the earliest observations in the
matching panel of Figure 3 (roughly 6-12, 40-105, 100-210 and 150-470 mg/L).

```{r mouse-sim}
mod_m <- readModelDb("Ji_2020_benapenem_mouse")
n_mouse <- 200
obs_times_m <- c(0, 0.083, 0.25, 0.5, seq(1, 24, by = 0.5))

make_mouse <- function(dose_mgkg, offset) {
  ids <- offset + seq_len(n_mouse)
  amt_ug <- dose_mgkg * mouse_wt_kg * 1000
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, evid = 1, amt = amt_ug),
    tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = obs_times_m) |> mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0)
  ) |>
    mutate(cmt = "central", DOSE_BENAPENEM_MGKG = dose_mgkg, treatment = paste(dose_mgkg, "mg/kg")) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
ev_m <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(mouse_doses), function(i) {
  make_mouse(mouse_doses[i], (i - 1) * n_mouse)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_m[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2020)
sim_m <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_m, ev_m, keep = c("treatment", "DOSE_BENAPENEM_MGKG"), returnType = "data.frame")
sim_m$treatment <- factor(sim_m$treatment, levels = paste(mouse_doses, "mg/kg"))
```

```{r mouse-vpc, fig.height = 6}
vpc_m <- sim_m |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(
    med = median(sim),
    lo = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    hi = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc_m, aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Total benapenem (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 (log scale) of Ji 2020: simulated median and 90% interval, 20 g mice."
  )
```

The paper reports that exposure rises less than in proportion to the dose.
The typical-value AUC per unit dose from the model should therefore fall
across the four dose levels. This check uses no random draws. In the mouse
model the effect is strong: clearance doubles at 58.4 mg/kg and rises about
8.5-fold at 233 mg/kg, so the typical AUC barely changes between the two
highest doses.

```{r mouse-dose-prop}
ev_typ_m <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(mouse_doses), function(i) {
  data.frame(
    id = i, time = c(0, seq(0, 48, by = 0.05)), evid = c(1, rep(0, 961)),
    amt = c(mouse_doses[i] * mouse_wt_kg * 1000, rep(0, 961)),
    cmt = "central", DOSE_BENAPENEM_MGKG = mouse_doses[i]
  )
}))
typ_m <- solve_typical(mod_m, ev_typ_m)
auc_typ_m <- typ_m |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2)) |>
  mutate(
    dose_mgkg = mouse_doses[id],
    auc_per_dose = auc / dose_mgkg
  )
knitr::kable(
  auc_typ_m |>
    transmute(dose_mgkg, auc = signif(auc, 3), auc_per_dose = signif(auc_per_dose, 3)) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Dose (mg/kg)" = dose_mgkg,
      "Typical AUC0-48 (mg*h/L)" = auc,
      "AUC per mg/kg" = auc_per_dose
    ),
  caption = "Typical-value total AUC by dose in 20 g mice (trapezoids on a 0.05 h grid)."
)
# Clearance doubles at 58.4 mg/kg and is about 8.5-fold higher at 233 mg/kg, so
# AUC per unit dose falls by a large factor from the lowest to the highest dose.
stopifnot(
  all(diff(auc_typ_m$auc_per_dose) < 0),
  auc_typ_m$auc_per_dose[1] / auc_typ_m$auc_per_dose[4] > 3
)
```

# Human PK (Figure 4)

The phase I cohort is represented by 200 virtual subjects per dose group. Body
weight is drawn from a normal distribution with mean 62.5 kg and SD 7 kg,
truncated to the observed range 51.8-78.3 kg (Table 1). Doses use the
estimated infusion duration `d1` (dose records with `rate = -2`), as in the
fitted data.
The plot uses the linear scale of the left-hand panels of Figure 4: with the
additive residual error, the lower 5% of simulated concentrations is below
zero by 24-48 h and cannot be drawn on a log scale.

```{r human-sim}
n_h <- 200
human_doses <- c(250, 500, 1000)
obs_times_h <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), seq(2.25, 12, by = 0.25), seq(12.5, 48, by = 0.5))))
set.seed(2020)
make_human <- function(dose, offset) {
  ids <- offset + seq_len(n_h)
  wt <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_h, 62.5, 7), 51.8), 78.3)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, evid = 1, amt = dose, rate = -2, WT = wt),
    tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = obs_times_h) |>
      mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, rate = 0) |>
      left_join(data.frame(id = ids, WT = wt), by = "id")
  ) |>
    mutate(cmt = "central", DOSE_BENAPENEM_MG = dose, treatment = paste(dose, "mg")) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
ev_h <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(human_doses), function(i) {
  make_human(human_doses[i], (i - 1) * n_h)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_h[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2020)
sim_h <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_h, ev_h, keep = c("treatment", "DOSE_BENAPENEM_MG"), returnType = "data.frame")
sim_h$treatment <- factor(sim_h$treatment, levels = paste(human_doses, "mg"))
```

```{r human-vpc, fig.height = 6}
vpc_h <- sim_h |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(
    med = median(sim),
    lo = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    hi = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc_h, aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Total benapenem (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 (linear scale) of Ji 2020: simulated median and 90% interval."
  )
```

The median simulated peak should match the peak of the median line in Figure
4 (about 45, 80 and 140 mg/L for 250, 500 and 1,000 mg, read from the plot).
The check is on the median, which a wrong clearance, volume, dose exponent or
infusion duration would move by tens of percent. The simulated peaks run about
12-14% above the figure at every dose. A constant offset like this is what to
expect from comparing a true peak with a VPC median that is binned over the
first sampling times, not from a structural error, which would change with
dose.

```{r human-peak}
peak_fig4 <- c("250 mg" = 45, "500 mg" = 80, "1000 mg" = 140)
peak_sim <- sim_h |>
  group_by(treatment, id) |>
  summarise(cmax = max(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(median_cmax = median(cmax), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    fig4 = peak_fig4[as.character(treatment)],
    pct_diff = round(100 * (median_cmax / fig4 - 1), 1)
  )
knitr::kable(
  peak_sim |>
    mutate(median_cmax = round(median_cmax, 1)) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Dose" = treatment,
      "Simulated median Cmax (mg/L)" = median_cmax,
      "Figure 4 peak (mg/L, digitised)" = fig4,
      "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
    )
)
stopifnot(all(abs(peak_sim$pct_diff) < 20))
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA results, so the PKNCA summary below has no published
column to compare against. It shows the less-than-proportional exposure: AUC
rises about 3-fold for a 4-fold dose increase.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_h |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

dose_df <- ev_h |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  transmute(id, time, amt, treatment = factor(treatment, levels = levels(sim_h$treatment)), duration = 0.404)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular", duration = "duration")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_sum <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life", "cl.obs")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
knitr::kable(
  nca_sum |>
    select(treatment, cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs, half.life, cl.obs) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Dose" = treatment,
      "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
      "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
      "AUC0-inf (mg*h/L)" = aucinf.obs,
      "t1/2 (h)" = half.life,
      "CL (L/h)" = cl.obs
    ),
  caption = "Median simulated NCA parameters by dose (total benapenem)."
)

auc_ratio <- nca_sum$aucinf.obs[nca_sum$treatment == "1000 mg"] /
  nca_sum$aucinf.obs[nca_sum$treatment == "250 mg"]
# Typical CL rises by 4^0.183 = 1.29 from 250 to 1000 mg, so the median AUC
# ratio is near 4 / 1.29 = 3.1; a dose-proportional model would give 4.
stopifnot(auc_ratio > 2.7, auc_ratio < 3.5)
```

# Probability of target attainment (Figures S57 and S60)

The authors simulated 250, 500 and 1,000 mg regimens given every 6, 8, 12 or
24 h as 0.5- to 3-h infusions. They computed %fT>MIC from the unbound
concentration and the PTA for targets of 40% and 60%. The dose in the captions
of Figures S55 to S60 is the total daily dose: "1,000 mg" given every 12 h
means 500 mg per infusion. %fT>MIC is taken over the first 24 h. That reading
reproduces all eight PTA curves of Figures S57 and S60 below. Giving the full
1,000 mg per infusion would put the q12h curves at about twice the MIC; using
steady state instead of the first day would move the q24h curves well away
from the published ones.

The simulation uses 200 subjects per regimen with the same weight
distribution as above. The dose covariate is the per-infusion amount, and each
infusion takes the nominal 0.5 h.

```{r pta-sim}
n_pta <- 200
pta_reg <- data.frame(tau = c(24, 12, 8, 6)) |>
  mutate(amt = 1000 * tau / 24, regimen = paste0("q", tau, "h"))
grid_pta <- seq(0, 24, by = 0.02)
set.seed(2021)
ev_pta <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pta_reg)), function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1) * n_pta + seq_len(n_pta)
  wt <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_pta, 62.5, 7), 51.8), 78.3)
  dose_times <- seq(0, 24 - pta_reg$tau[i], by = pta_reg$tau[i])
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = dose_times) |>
      mutate(evid = 1, amt = pta_reg$amt[i], rate = pta_reg$amt[i] / 0.5),
    tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = grid_pta) |> mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, rate = 0)
  ) |>
    left_join(data.frame(id = ids, WT = wt), by = "id") |>
    mutate(cmt = "central", DOSE_BENAPENEM_MG = pta_reg$amt[i], regimen = pta_reg$regimen[i])
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2021)
sim_pta <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_h, ev_pta, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  filter(time < 24)

mic_grid <- seq(0.2, 4.4, by = 0.1)
ft <- sim_pta |>
  group_by(regimen, id) |>
  summarise(
    ft = list(vapply(mic_grid, function(m) 100 * mean(Cunbound > m), numeric(1))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::unnest_longer(ft, indices_to = "k") |>
  mutate(mic = mic_grid[k])
pta <- tidyr::crossing(ft, target = c(40, 60)) |>
  group_by(regimen, target, mic) |>
  summarise(pta = 100 * mean(ft >= target), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = c("q24h", "q12h", "q8h", "q6h")))
```

```{r pta-plot}
ggplot(pta, aes(mic, pta, linetype = factor(target))) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  labs(
    x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "Probability of target attainment (%)", linetype = "%fT>MIC target",
    caption = "Replicates the 0.5 h infusion curves of Figures S57 and S60 of Ji 2020 (1,000 mg/day)."
  )
```

The MIC at which PTA crosses 50% sits at the centre of the exposure
distribution, so it checks the model's structure rather than the tails. The
published values below are read from Figures S57 and S60 by interpolating
between the plotted points on either side of 50%.

```{r pta-compare}
mic50_pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~target, ~mic50_pub,
  "q24h", 40, 2.73, "q12h", 40, 3.10, "q8h", 40, 3.32, "q6h", 40, 3.53,
  "q24h", 60, 1.50, "q12h", 60, 2.18, "q8h", 60, 2.50, "q6h", 60, 2.71
)
mic50_sim <- pta |>
  group_by(regimen, target) |>
  arrange(mic, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    mic50_sim = {
      j <- which(pta < 50)[1]
      mic[j - 1] + (50 - pta[j - 1]) * (mic[j] - mic[j - 1]) / (pta[j] - pta[j - 1])
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(regimen = as.character(regimen))
mic50 <- left_join(mic50_pub, mic50_sim, by = c("regimen", "target")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = round(100 * (mic50_sim / mic50_pub - 1), 1), mic50_sim = round(mic50_sim, 2))
knitr::kable(
  mic50 |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Regimen (1,000 mg/day)" = regimen,
      "%fT>MIC target" = target,
      "Published MIC at PTA 50% (mg/L)" = mic50_pub,
      "Simulated MIC at PTA 50% (mg/L)" = mic50_sim,
      "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
    )
)
# A wrong clearance, binding constant or dose reading moves these by tens of
# percent (giving the full 1,000 mg per q12h infusion doubles them).
stopifnot(all(abs(mic50$pct_diff) < 12))

pta_cutoff <- pta$pta[pta$regimen == "q24h" & pta$target == 60 & abs(pta$mic - 1) < 1e-9]
```

The authors chose 1,000 mg every 24 h as a 0.5-h infusion and a 60% target,
which gives a PK/PD cutoff of 1 mg/L (the highest MIC with PTA of at least
90%). The packaged model gives a PTA of `r round(pta_cutoff)`% at 1 mg/L for
that regimen.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Mouse body weight.** The mouse model's dose covariate is in mg/kg and its
  volumes are in mL per mouse, so the dose records need the amount per mouse.
  The paper does not report mouse weights. This vignette assumes 20 g, which
  puts the simulated concentrations on the scale of Figure 3. Users should
  enter each mouse's actual dose in ug.
* **IIV scale.** Tables 3 and 4 print IIV_CL and IIV_V1 as 36.5, 10.5 and 7.6
  without defining them. They are read as CV percentages and converted with
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. Reading them as `100 x sqrt(omega^2)` instead
  would change the variances by less than 7% (mouse) and 1% (human).
* **Residual error.** Equation 6 is the combined form
  `Cobs = Cpred x (1 + eps1) + eps2`; the proportional SD (7.4%, 30.1%) and
  the human additive SD (0.233, read as mg/L, the plotted concentration unit)
  are taken as standard deviations. The mouse additive term was fixed to 0
  and is omitted.
* **Protein-binding parameters are fixed.** They were fitted to in vitro
  binding data in a separate step before the PK models were built (Methods,
  "Protein binding model"), so they enter both model files as fixed values.
  The binding fits' own proportional errors (5.4% mouse, 16.3% human,
  Table 5) are not part of the PK models.
* **Infusion duration.** The human model estimated the infusion duration
  (D1 = 0.404 h) instead of using the nominal 0.5 h. Dose records with
  `rate = -2` use it; records with an explicit rate or duration use theirs,
  as the PTA simulation does.
* **Dose covariate in multiple-dose use.** `DOSE_BENAPENEM_MG` is the amount
  per infusion. The PTA comparison above shows that the authors used the
  per-infusion amount, not the daily total, when they split a daily dose.
* **Human weight distribution for simulation.** The paper does not describe
  the simulated population. A truncated normal (mean 62.5 kg, SD 7 kg,
  51.8-78.3 kg) approximates the phase I cohort.
* **Not packaged.** The mouse %fT>MIC versus change in log10 CFU/g
  relationships (Figures S1 to S12) are linear trend lines with no reported
  parameters. Ertapenem was used as a comparator with PK data from the
  literature (Table S1), but no ertapenem model parameters are reported, so
  Figure 7 cannot be reproduced.

## Errata

* The Figure 3 caption labels the mouse dose groups "1.9-mg", "14.6-mg",
  "58.4-mg" and "233-mg"; the Methods give these doses in mg/kg.
* The Results text gives the unit of V1 in the mouse model as "hours"; Table 3
  gives mL.
* Equation 6's legend calls eps1 and eps2 the additive and proportional
  errors, respectively. In the equation as printed, eps1 is the proportional
  and eps2 the additive term, and the model follows the equation.
